chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The one who has washed the deceased performs ghusl. If a person kisses the deceased after his death while he is still warm, then there is no ghusl upon him. But if he touches him and kisses him after he has become cold, then ghusl is obligatory upon him. There is no harm in touching him after the ghusl and kissing him.

So what these reports contain of the wording of command regarding ghusl from touching the deceased and washing the dead indicates obligation, because a command by its apparent meaning entails obligation, and one does not depart from obligation to recommendation except with evidence.

key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person whose body is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْوُجُوبِ: legal obligation indicated by the wording of the command
key_terms.تَغْسِيلِ الْأَمْوَاتِ: washing the dead as part of funerary rites
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required in specific cases connected to the deceased
key_terms.مَسِّ الْمَيِّتِ: touching the body of the deceased, which may entail ghusl

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory after touching or washing a deceased person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report states that ghusl is required for the one who washes the deceased, and for one who touches and kisses the deceased after the body has become cold. It also clarifies that if the deceased is still warm, ghusl is not required, and the concluding legal discussion affirms that the command here indicates obligation unless there is evidence otherwise.
